exercise1.prompt: Long to Wide with pivot: Spread the months across

hiddenCases.name: a single month gives a single column
several people share the same columns

exercise1.hint: index is what stays down the side, columns is what spreads across the top, values fills the cells. sorted() on the result keeps the answer stable.

exercise2.prompt: Long to Wide with pivot: Spread a table that has duplicates

hiddenCases.name: names become the rows and months the columns
two names and two months make a 2x2 grid
a table with no duplicates still works

exercise2.hint: pivot raises on duplicate index/column pairs. pivot_table with aggfunc="mean" answers the question pivot could not, then .shape gives the grid size.

choices: Long back to wide — one row per entity again
questions.explain: The inverse of melt, and the shape a report table usually wants.

questions.prompt: pivot raises "Index contains duplicate entries". Why?
choices: Two rows want the same cell, and a cell holds one value
questions.explain: It is a question pivot cannot answer on its own, not a broken table.

questions.prompt: What fixes that, when the duplicates are legitimate?
questions.explain: The aggfunc says what to do with the two values — a decision you should be making anyway.

questions.prompt: After pivot, where is the index column?
questions.explain: reset_index() puts it back as a column when you want a plain table.
